I am an old woman of 80 years, farming this small piece of land my family owns. I plant my cassava and yam together as my mother taught me, using the cuttings and seed yams I saved from last harvest. I cannot afford the chemical fertilizer from town, and these root crops do not need it much anyway — I put the goat droppings and kitchen ash on the mounds. My grandchildren help me weed and harvest, so I do not need to hire anyone.
